CveFindings.Name: Microsoft: CBC Padding Oracle in Azure Blob Storage Encryption Library
CveFindings.Description: [CVE-2022-30187](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-64x4-9hc6-r2h6). Severity: MEDIUM. Azure.Storage.Blobs 12.9.1 matches NuGet range < 12.13.0. Upgrade to 12.13.0 or later and follow the advisory's client-side encryption migration guidance. Package-version finding; client-side encryption exploitability is not established. Collection: dotnet list package --include-transitive --format json failed because Microsoft.WebApplication.targets is missing; packages.config supplied all 34 declared packages, including NuGet-distributed JavaScript. Public GitHub Advisory REST queries used batches of 30 and 4, followed pagination, filtered NuGet package identities and installed-version ranges, excluded three withdrawn advisories, and deduplicated CVEs. Thirteen active version matches were found. Coverage does not establish deployment state, framework/OS patching, dependencies absent from the manifest, or runtime exploitability.

CweFindings.Name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync uses attacker-selected Request.Files.Count as the loop bound without a per-request file-count/work cap. Each accepted multipart entry performs a sequential storage upload. With the initialized/configured container and an existing readable local source filename (the local-path bug), many small multipart entries can repeat the same source read and generate many unique blob writes, amplifying request CPU/I/O, storage transactions and occupied request lifetime. Web.config sets maxRequestLength=2100000000 and executionTimeout=12000000; these do not constrain file count. Upstream IIS/proxy limits may reduce input size; no bypass of those limits or quantified DoS is claimed.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Initialization
CweFindings.Description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource, which might leave the resource in an unexpected state when it is accessed or used.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController stores blobContainer in a static field but only initializes it inside the independently routed Index action. A direct POST to DeleteAll after application startup/recycle, before any Index request reaches line 65, dereferences null at GetBlobs; UploadAsync with a multipart file similarly dereferences it at line 108. RouteConfig permits these direct action routes and neither startup nor the actions initialize the resource. The exception is caught and returns Error, so the confirmed impact is request-level functionality failure due to initialization ordering, not a process crash, cross-account access, or sustained denial of service.

CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
CweFindings.Description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.
CweFindings.Explanation: The application gives every reachable caller the controller's storage-account deletion capability: DeleteImage and DeleteAll are public POST actions with no authorization check, no controller-level authorization, and no global authorization filter. After Index initializes the configured container, an anonymous POST /Home/DeleteAll enumerates and deletes every block blob; DeleteImage permits individual deletion based on a supplied URI basename. Public viewing of gallery photos does not require public destructive access. This finding concerns gallery integrity, not a claim that intentional public photo viewing alone is insecure. External IIS/network authentication could restrict exposure, but no such protection is present in repository configuration. Primary weakness is missing authorization; reported under this requested permission category because the effective application permission grants destructive access to anonymous callers.

CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging
CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.DeleteImage and DeleteAll perform security-critical storage deletion without recording the requester, target objects, deletion result or operation identifier. Success redirects; exception paths only render message/stack trace in the response and do not persist an application audit event. Thus the anonymous destructive operations identified above leave no application-level audit trail. Hosting request logs and optional Azure diagnostic logging were not available and may provide partial external evidence; this finding does not claim those external logs are absent.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync passes attacker-controlled multipart files[i].FileName directly to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path), which opens that path on the server instead of reading the uploaded InputStream. After Index initializes the shared container, a crafted multipart filename naming a process-readable server file causes that file's contents to be copied into blob storage. Index lists blob URIs and creates new containers with PublicAccessType.Blob, exposing copied data when public access is permitted. No authentication or path confinement is present. Requires a configured writable storage account and a readable existing target. This and CWE-23/CWE-36 are three classifications of one root cause, not three independent defects.

CweFindings.Name: Relative Path Traversal
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync sends the unmodified multipart filename to the server-local path overload of BlobClient.UploadAsync. A crafted filename such as ../target.txt or ..\target.txt traverses relative to the server process working directory when the target exists and the process can read it. GetRandomBlobName only transforms the destination blob name; it does not sanitize the local source path. The resulting blob is discoverable through Index. Same root cause as CWE-22; exploitation depends on working-directory layout, storage configuration, and file permissions.

CweFindings.Name: Absolute Path Traversal
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: A manually crafted multipart filename such as C:\Windows\win.ini reaches BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path) unchanged in HomeController.UploadAsync. On the intended Windows host this selects an absolute server-local file rather than uploaded content, and copies a process-readable target to the configured blob container. There is no root/path allowlist. Same root cause as CWE-22; requires a successful Index initialization, storage access, and target read permission.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: DisplayFilesToUpload concatenates File.name into markup and assigns that markup to FilesToUpload.innerHTML on the file input onchange event. On filesystems permitting angle brackets (for example Linux), an attacker-supplied file named .png injects an image/event handler into the application's DOM when the victim selects that file. This is user-assisted DOM XSS: it requires the victim to obtain and select an attacker-named file and a platform/browser preserving that name; it is not an unauthenticated remote reflected/stored XSS claim. The injection occurs before the upload request, independently of the server upload bug.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
CweFindings.Description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync lets attacker-controlled multipart FileName choose the source resource passed to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path), a server-local file read. A crafted filename identifying an existing readable local file copies that resource into the gallery container instead of using the posted file bytes. Requires configured storage and initialized blobContainer. This is the same root cause classified as CWE-22/CWE-23/CWE-36 in the file/path artifact; it is not an additional independent exploit.
